new_groups.label: Hamet Caramalli's claim on the United States, 1806

Contains those four groups.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's message of 13 January on Hamet Caramalli
new_groups.definition: Printings of President Jefferson's message to Congress of 13 January 1806: 'I lay before Congress the application of Hamet Caramalli, elder brother of the reigning bashaw of Tripoli, soliciting from the United States attention to his services and sufferings in the late war against that state'. The executive's own account of its dealings with him.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The convention between William Eaton and Hamet Caramalli

ARTICLE I. There shall be a firm and perpetual peace and free intercourse' between the two. An agreement, as the message printed it.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Hamet's letter to the President
new_groups.definition: Printings of a letter from Hamet ('Achmet Bashaw') to the President, sent to Congress with the message of 13 January 1806: 'For nearly eleven years, I have been labouring under the weight of misfortune'. His own account of the war against Tripoli and of his part in it with General Eaton.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Senate committee's report on Hamet Caramalli, 17 March

new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Trade with St. Domingo: the French complaints and the act of 28 February 1806

new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's message with the French complaints on trade with St. Domingo

new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The act of 28 February 1806 suspending trade with parts of St. Domingo

new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: British seizures and impressment: papers sent to Congress, January 1806

new_groups.label: The President's message of 17 January on British seizures and impressment

new_groups.label: The thirtieth bulletin of the Grand Army

new_groups.label: The Emperor's proclamation to the army after the battle

new_groups.label: "Serious Questions to Mr. Madison" on General Miranda's expedition

new_groups.label: The treaty of Pressburg between Austria and France
new_groups.definition: Printings of the treaty of peace between Austria and France signed at Pressburg on 26 December 1805: 'His majesty the emperor of Germany and Austria, and his majesty the emperor of the French, king of Italy, equally animated with a desire to put an end to the calamities of war'. Some papers printed it with the Emperor Napoleon's act of ratification before it. A treaty.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The House's secret journal on Spanish affairs, published in April
new_groups.definition: Printings of the journal of the House of Representatives' proceedings with closed doors in December 1805 and January 1806 on the President's message of 6 December 1805 about Spain, made public at the beginning of April 1806 when 'the injunction of secrecy' was taken off: the committee's report ('The committee have beheld with just indignation the hostile spirit manifested by the court of Madrid'), the resolutions and the votes. Six papers printed the journal as the National Intelligencer gave it; three printed a shorter account with the report or the resolutions. An official record.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A Bremen letter on the sentences of the Austrian officers
new_groups.definition: Printings of a paragraph from London papers of February 1806: 'A private letter from Bremen of the 11th inst. contains the following article, relative to the sentences passed on the officers whose conduct produced the recent misfortunes to the House of Austria'. A report at second hand, from a private letter.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: General Miranda's expedition, 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings about the expedition that General Francisco de Miranda fitted out at New York in the ship Leander for the coast of Caracas, as the papers printed them through 1806: questions put to the Secretary of State in February, a letter from on board the Leander in April, Miranda's proclamation of 28 June, and a report of the expedition's defeat in November. Contains those four groups.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A letter from on board the Leander at Jacmel, 1 March
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter 'from a gentleman on board the Leander', dated Jacmel, 1 March 1806: 'General Miranda has explained to us his plan'. One member of the expedition's own account.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: General Miranda's proclamation of 28 June: 'Friends and Countrymen'
new_groups.definition: Printings of the proclamation that General Miranda issued on 28 June 1806 ('published at Trinidad', in one paper's words): 'FRIENDS AND COUNTRYMEN, The glorious opportunity now presents itself of relieving from oppression and arbitrary government, a people who are worthy of a better fate'. The expedition's own appeal.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: 'Miranda defeated': Captain Foster's report from Trinidad
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Boston paragraph of November 1806 headed 'MIRANDA DEFEATED': Captain Foster, arrived from Trinidad, 'informs, that three days previous to his sailing, a Mr. Taylor, who had embarked in the expedition with Miranda, reached that place with the unpleasant intelligence of their defeat'. A report at second hand.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's message on Tunis, April 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings of President Jefferson's message to Congress on the dispute with Tunis, read in the House on 14 April 1806: 'During the blockade of Tripoli by the squadron of the U. S. a small cruiser, under the flag of Tunis, with two prizes' tried to enter the port. The executive's own account.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The act of 18 April 1806 prohibiting certain British goods
new_groups.definition: Printings of the act of Congress approved on 18 April 1806 'To prohibit the importation of certain goods, wares and merchandise': from 15 November 'it shall not be lawful to import into the United States, or the territories thereof, from any port or place situated in Great Britain or Ireland' the goods it lists. A law.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Leander off New York, 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings after a cannon shot from the British ship Leander killed an American seaman near the entrance of New York harbour on 25 April 1806, which the President's proclamation calls 'a murder': the resolutions of a meeting at New York and the President's proclamation of 3 May. Contains those two groups.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Resolutions of a New York meeting after the Leander shot
new_groups.definition: Printings of the resolutions of 'a meeting of Federal Republicans' at the Tontine Coffee House, New York, in late April 1806, called 'to take into consideration the defenceless state of our harbor': 'Resolved, That the citizens of the U. S. are of right, and according to the constitution and laws of the land, entitled to the enjoyment of life, liberty, and property'. A party meeting's own resolutions.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's proclamation of 3 May against the Leander, Cambrian and Driver
new_groups.definition: Printings of President Jefferson's proclamation of 3 May 1806: Henry Whitby, commanding the British armed vessel Leander, had by a cannon shot within the waters of the United States near New York committed what it calls 'a murder'; the Leander, the Cambrian and the Driver are to leave American waters, and the President will 'forbid all intercourse with the said armed vessels' if they do not. An official document; the charge is the President's. The excerpts end before the name of the man killed.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Emperor Napoleon's speech opening the Legislative Body, March 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings of the speech of the Emperor Napoleon at the opening of the French Legislative Body in March 1806: 'Since your last session, the greatest part of Europe has entered into a coalition with England. My armies have never ceased to conquer'. A head of state's own account.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A Philadelphia report of movements in St. Domingo, May 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Philadelphia paragraph of 10 May 1806: 'We learn from a gentleman who arrived in this city a day or two ago, from St. Domingo, that at the time of his departure there were very general movements among the subjects of the black emperor Dessalines'; the cause was not known, 'but it was said that some advices had been received by way of Jamaica'. A traveller's report at second hand, in the paper's words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Norfolk, May 1806: 'The French Admiral Linois taken'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a Norfolk paragraph of May 1806 headed 'The French Admiral Linois taken': the British frigate Tartar, arrived in Hampton Roads from Bermuda, had boarded the American ship Hunter from Lisbon, whose people had seen the French ship Marengo, 'Admiral Linois', and the frigate Belle Poule with the squadron of Sir John Borlase Warren, 'captured by Sir John'. A report passed on from ship to ship.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Captain Dodge's report from Cape François, June 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings of a New York paragraph of 9 June 1806 headed 'MASSACRE AT CAPE FRANCOIS': Captain Dodge of the schooner Mary Ann, arrived from Cape François, reported 'that on the 14th and 15th of May, a general massacre of all the remaining white inhabitants of Cape Francois took place, and it was said, generally, throughout that part of this ill-fated island under the dominion of Dessalines'. A shipmaster's report, partly hearsay, in the paper's words.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: General Heath declines to be Lieutenant Governor of Massachusetts
new_groups.definition: Printings of the letter of William Heath to the Senate and House of Representatives of Massachusetts, June 1806: 'I have been notified by a very respectable committee of both Houses, that I have been elected Lieutenant Governor of the Commonwealth'; he declines the office. A public man's own statement.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A Swedish bulletin: the Prussians cross into Lauenburg
new_groups.definition: Printings of a 'Swedish bulletin' from the headquarters of the Swedish army, April 1806, from London papers: reports 'received from adjutant general count Lowenhielm' said the Prussians had taken several villages near Lauenburg, and on the 23rd 'the Prussians passed the Lauenburg frontier'. One army's own account.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: A letter from Detroit of 1 June on councils of the Indian nations
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter from a gentleman at Detroit, dated 1 June 1806: traders had reported to the acting governor 'the frequent secret councils held by the Indians', and the writer says 'We are now no longer in doubt, that the Indians are preparing to commence war against the United States'. One American writer's account of traders' reports, with his forecast.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Fox's note to Monroe on the blockade from the Elbe to Brest
new_groups.definition: Printings of the note of Charles James Fox, the British Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, to James Monroe, the American minister (Downing Street, May 1806): the King 'has thought fit to direct that the necessary measures should be taken for the blockade of the coasts, rivers and ports from the river Elbe to the port of Brest, both inclusive'. The British government's notice.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Louis Napoleon proclaimed King of Holland, 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings of the proclamation of Louis Napoleon as King of Holland (June 1806), 'read this day to the military, and announced to the people': 'Louis Napoleon, by the Grace of God and the constitutional laws of the state, King of Holland, to all who shall see and read this, greeting'. A ruler's own proclamation.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Spanish and American troops near the Sabine, 1806
new_groups.definition: Letters printed from September to November 1806 on Spanish troops east of the Sabine and the American army sent against them: a letter of 2 August headed 'HOSTILE APPEARANCE', a Natchitoches letter on Mr. Freeman's exploring party, and a letter of General Wilkinson. Each is one writer's account, from the American side. Contains those three groups.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: 'Hostile appearance': a letter of 2 August on Spanish troops
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter to the editor of a Natchez paper, dated 2 August 1806 and headed 'HOSTILE APPEARANCE': 'On or about the 18th of July ult. a detachment of Spanish troops' came toward Natchitoches. The papers give the writer's place as Natchez or Natchitoches. One writer's account.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Natchitoches, 26 August: Mr. Freeman's party turned back
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract from Natchitoches, 26 August 1806: 'Mr. Freeman returned to this place on Saturday last, after having ascended 430 miles above this place, where the Spaniards had been waiting for him'. One writer's account of the exploring party sent up the Red River.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: General Wilkinson's letter from the Rapids of Red River, 19 September
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter of General Wilkinson, dated Rapids of Red River, 19 September 1806: 'My orders, and the conduct of the Mexicans, are so much at variance'; 'I fear you will be informed blood has been spilt'. The American commander's own account, with his forecast.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The return of Lewis and Clark, 1806
new_groups.definition: The first printed news of the return of Captain Lewis, Captain Clark and their party to St. Louis from the Pacific, in September 1806: the National Intelligencer's announcement and Captain Clark's letter to his brother. Contains those two groups.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The National Intelligencer announces Captain Lewis's arrival at St. Louis
new_groups.definition: Printings of the National Intelligencer's paragraph of 27 October 1806: 'It is with the sincerest pleasure, that we announce to our fellow citizens, the arrival of CAPTAIN LEWIS, with his exploring party, at St. Louis'; the President had a letter from him dated 23 September. The government paper's report.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Captain Clark's letter to his brother, St. Louis, 23 September
new_groups.definition: Printings of Captain Clark's letter to his brother, dated St. Louis, 23 September 1806: 'We arrived at this place at 12 o'clock to-day, from the Pacific Ocean, where we remained during the last winter, near the entrance of the Columbia river'. One of the party's own account of the journey.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Francis II gives up the crown of the German Empire
new_groups.definition: Printings of the declaration of Francis II, emperor of Austria, giving up 'the high office of emperor of Germany', from the Paris Moniteur of 14 August 1806: 'Since the peace of Presburg all our attention and all our care have been employed to fulfil with scrupulous fidelity all the engagements' of that treaty. A ruler's own declaration.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: London, September 1806: Buenos Ayres captured
new_groups.definition: Printings of a London paragraph of September 1806: 'The official news of the capture of Buenos Ayres is received. It capitulated on the 27th of June. There fell into the hands of the English 1,291,338 dollars'. A report from the British side.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Colonel Burr's enterprise in the papers, November 1806
new_groups.definition: The first widely printed items on Aaron Burr's enterprise in the West, November 1806: a Chillicothe report of an affidavit against him in Kentucky, and the President's proclamation of 27 November against a military expedition against the dominions of Spain. Contains those two groups.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: Chillicothe, 13 November: the Kentucky affidavit against Colonel Burr
new_groups.definition: Printings of a paragraph from the Scioto Gazette (Chillicothe, 13 November 1806) headed 'IMPORTANT COMMUNICATION': 'By a gentleman of the highest respectability from Kentucky, we are furnished with the following intelligence'; the substance of an affidavit of the United States attorney for Kentucky (printed 'Davies' or 'Daveiss') that Aaron Burr 'had formed an Association for making war against Spain, invading Mexico, and forming a distinct Empire in the Western country'. An allegation, reported at second hand.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's proclamation of 27 November against a military expedition
new_groups.definition: Printings of President Jefferson's proclamation of 27 November 1806: 'WHEREAS information has been received that sundry persons, citizens of the United States, or residents within the same are conspiring and confederating together to begin and set on foot, provide and prepare the means for a military expedition or enterprise against the dominions of Spain'; it warns citizens 'to withdraw from the same without delay'. It names no one. An official document.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's message of 3 December on suspending the act
new_groups.definition: Printings of President Jefferson's message to Congress of 3 December 1806: 'I have the satisfaction to inform you that the negotiation depending between the United States and the government of Great Britain is proceeding in a spirit of friendship', and that 'a temporary suspension of the act of last session, prohibiting certain importations, would, as a mark of candid disposition on our part' help it. The executive's own account and request.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The President's annual message of 2 December 1806
new_groups.definition: Printings of President Jefferson's annual message to Congress of 2 December 1806: 'It would have given me, fellow citizens, great satisfaction to announce, in the moment of your meeting, that the difficulties in our foreign relations, existing at the time of your last separation, had been amicably and justly terminated'. The executive's own account of the year.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The Hague, 17 October 1806: war between France and Prussia
new_groups.definition: Printings of a paragraph from Dutch papers (the Hague, 17 October 1806), translated in New York: 'Last night his excellency the Secretary of State received the important intelligence, that hostilities have commenced between the French and Prussians'. A first report of the war, through the Dutch papers.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1806 printings, checked against the scan.

dispositions_summary.method: Pages were taken by their printed dates (year_search_pages.py --printed-dates), so the 98 Kentucky Gazette issues filed under 1808 count as the 1806 issues they are, and the 7 filed under 1806 that print 1804 mastheads are left out: 4,381 pages in 12 papers. The automatic families first printed in 1806 that reach 4 or more papers, long-running ones included (story_items.py --long-running), were split into single printed items (items.json); the same script was also run with year 1805 over the 1806 pages (items_from_1805.json). Two AI reviewers read the items of each half of the year and proposed the stories; each item's printings were looked for with phrase searches over all pages of 1806 in both transcriptions (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json), and every hit was read. Papers with pages in a story's weeks but no printing were searched with loose keywords, and the scan pages whose RevX text is filed under another page were read in the CA transcription. Every admitted printing was then checked against its page scan (SCAN_PROTOCOL.md, scan_points.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: As for 1776, 1807 and 1808: every single item printed in 9 or more newspapers was admitted, except digests of unrelated paragraphs and lists or chains of acts. Items in 7 or 8 papers were chosen to cover the months and the main kinds of news. Stories are counted item by item; where one publication holds several documents, or several documents belong to one affair, each is its own group under a parent story. Every group reaches 7 papers. Every story alike: reports on slavery, Native nations and St. Domingo were chosen by the same rule and are described by the kind of text and whose account it is, in the papers' own words. Stories that turn on private persons were not admitted; they are listed for the owner's decision.

counted_item_by_item.Printed forms counted together: The speech opening Parliament with two printed extracts; the Detroit letter with one shorter version; General Wilkinson's letter with a Cincinnati paragraph that quotes it; the Chillicothe report on Burr with one shorter version; the House's secret journal with three shorter accounts.
counted_item_by_item.Enclosures counted apart: The Eaton–Hamet convention, Hamet's letter and Monroe's letter to Lord Mulgrave were printed in other issues than the messages that sent them, so each is its own group under its parent story.
counted_item_by_item.Lists and chains of acts: The weekly 'Acts passed at the first session of the Ninth Congress' and laws printed by authority share titles and the enacting formula; each act was counted by its own text, not as one item.

not_admitted.Stories that turn on private persons: The arrests of Samuel G. Ogden and Colonel William S. Smith in the Miranda affair (7 papers), the funeral procession for the man killed by the Leander's shot (about 7), and Colonel Smith's letters with the Marquis de Casa Yrujo about his son (7): left for the owner's decision.
not_admitted.Set aside as repeats of an affair or mon: The list of prisoners taken in Miranda's schooners, the Jamaica report of Miranda's landing near Coro, Miranda's proclamation at Coro, the Corporation of New York's memorial on the Leander, the Natchez paragraph on Bayou Pierre, General Eaton's statement on Burr, the Enquirer's communication on the secret proceedings, the paragraph on Monroe and Pinkney, George III's declaration on Hanover, General Stuart's dispatch on Maida and Captain Foster's news of d'Oubril's treaty.
